Evidence Proof: X-Powered-By: PHP/8.3.37
What this means: Checks if Server header reveals software names and exact version numbers (e.g., Apache/2.4.41).
Why it matters: Detailed version information allows attackers to look up specific CVE exploits for that exact version.
How to Reproduce & Verify Fix · Confirmed Reproducible
Observed: HTTP 200 — X-Powered-By: PHP/8.3.37 (Technology/version disclosed — remove this header)
  1. Send GET request to https://www.toprelatos.com/.
  2. Observe the indicator (HTTP 200 — X-Powered-By: PHP/8.3.37 (Technology/version disclosed — remove this header)) on HTTP 200.
  3. Apply the remediation, then replay GET https://www.toprelatos.com/ and re-run check "server-disclosure" to confirm status transitions to SAFE and the triggering indicator no longer appears.
curl -i -sS --resolve 'www.toprelatos.com:443:104.21.78.35' 'https://www.toprelatos.com/'
Recommendation
Disable server signatures (e.g., 'ServerTokens Prod' in Apache, 'server_tokens off' in Nginx) and remove headers like 'X-Powered-By' to prevent version disclosure.

[SECSCAN platform control, not target defense] DNS pin mismatch for "www.toprelatos.com": resolved [188.114.96.0, 188.114.97.0] not in pinned set [104.21.78.35, 172.67.215.185]
What this means: Tests if user inputs in query parameters are reflected unsanitized in the HTML page body.
Why it matters: XSS allows attackers to execute malicious JavaScript in victims' browsers, stealing cookies and session tokens.
How to Reproduce & Verify Fix · Recorded Trigger Trace
Observed: [SECSCAN platform control, not target defense] DNS pin mismatch for "www.toprelatos.com": resolved [188.114.96.0, 188.114.97.0] not in pinned set [104.21.78.35, 172.67.215.185]

  2. Observe the indicator ([SECSCAN platform control, not target defense] DNS pin mismatch for "www.toprelatos.com": resolved [188.114.96.0, 188.114.97.0] not in pinned set [104.21.78.35, 172.67.215.185]).
  3. Apply the remediation, then replay GET https://www.toprelatos.com/wp-json/oembed/1.0/embed?url=%3Cscript%3Ealert%28%27xss-probe-3wxaub%27%29%3C%2Fscript%3E and re-run check "xss" to confirm status transitions to SAFE and the triggering indicator no longer appears.

Sanitize and HTML-encode all user input before outputting it into web pages, and deploy a strong CSP.

Client-Side API Communication & Endpoint Discovery
api communication API Security CWE-200 A05:2021-Security Misconfiguration CVSS 5.3 PoE L0 not_assessed
Pages (1):
  • https://www.toprelatos.com
No client-side API communication detected (traditional_web)
What this means: Inspects Single Page Application (SPA) HTML, JavaScript bundles (Angular, React, Vue, Next.js), runtime configuration files (/assets/config.json, /config.json, /env.js), and CSP connect-src directives to map client-to-API communication, discover backend REST/GraphQL/WebSocket endpoints, and detect unauthenticated API data exposure or insecure API configurations.
Why it matters: Modern SPAs communicate directly with same-origin or external backend APIs via Angular HttpClient, Fetch, Axios, or GraphQL. Hardcoded development/localhost API URLs, plaintext HTTP API endpoints on HTTPS pages, exposed runtime config files, or unauthenticated JSON API endpoints can leak sensitive customer data, credentials, and internal service topology.
Recommendation
Use environment-specific production builds (e.g., Angular environment.prod.ts without dev proxy.conf.json localhost URLs), enforce HTTPS for all API origins, require authentication on sensitive REST/GraphQL endpoints, remove secrets from public /assets/config.json files, and restrict allowed API origins via Content-Security-Policy connect-src and strict CORS policies.
✅ SAFE NONE

What this means: Passively and safely inspects PHP targets for the php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) session.upload_progress multipart PHPSESSID fixation, raw filename session injection, var_destroy UAF, and FPM PS(serializer) handler mismatch conditions.
Why it matters: In PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11, the rfc1867 session.upload_progress handler accepts PHPSESSID from multipart POST form data ignoring session.use_only_cookies and writes raw filenames into session files, enabling LFI-to-RCE and deserialization RCE.

No Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) arithmetic evaluation detected.
What this means: Tests URL query parameters with non-destructive arithmetic template expressions across Jinja2/Twig/Pebble ({{7919*13}}), Freemarker/Spring EL/Thymeleaf (${7919*13}), and ERB/EJS (<%= 7919*13 %>), verifying that the server evaluates the expression to 102947 without reflecting the un-evaluated formula.
Why it matters: When user input is concatenated directly into a server-side template string before rendering, attackers can execute arbitrary template expressions and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
